_comment: Cycle-charge stance demo (seed 12345): box-select the player's two cavalry regiments (right of the line, ~x 1027 and 1356, y 300), press J to arm the Cycle charge stance, then right-click the enemy Infantry regiment at (291,880). The horse charges in, lands its momentum hit, then peels back to a standoff and charges AGAIN -- the caracole loop -- instead of grinding in melee once the charge bonus is spent. The HUD flashes 'Cycle charge' when J is pressed and the order cursor turns violet.

overlap.reason: Charging cavalry peels back and compresses laterally during cycle-charge caracole maneuver before re-forming. uid 7 (team 1 archers) is downstream of team 1's own cavalry, which sits at the reference depth ratio (2.81) and now pivots its early formed turn at 0.6 pace: the two runs diverge from tick 19 and by tick 900 the archers are in a different engagement (measured on the same machine at the catalog cadence: main uid7 overlap worst 30.5 wu, branch 1.98 wu against the 2.25 floor; main uid6 overlap 0.15 wu and shape residual 59.4 wu, both cleared on the branch). The archers block itself is not deep by the metric (ratio 1.49, fraction 1.0), so its own pace and corridor band are unchanged. uid8 IS that team 1 cavalry itself (depth ratio 505.96/(40wu file pitch x 4.5) = 2.810913, exactly the reference case, frac 0.6): its own reduced pivot rate changes its whole AI chase trajectory against the player's cavalry (target_enemy_uid cycling 3->4->2 as it repeatedly re-faces), so it covers far less net distance over the clip than on main (main reaches x=256/y=501 by tick 1300, closing to melee and reaching FIGHTING at tick 1200; this branch only reaches x=842/y=576 by tick 1300, never engaging) -- the same divergence already responsible for uid7's exemption, now also visible as an overlap dip in uid8's own bodies at the clip's final sample (main nnd_min 14.19wu at tick 1300 vs this branch's 4.49wu against the 5.0wu floor). Downstream chase-trajectory chaos from the intended pivot-rate derate, not a standing formation defect; measured on both worktrees at the catalog cadence. Re-measured while investigating the uid8 shape_residual finding below: still needed (nnd_min 4.49wu, unchanged, under the 5.0wu floor -- the analyzer's own stale_exempt flag reads false for this uid/metric pair).

shape_residual.reason: Charging cavalry block deforms during cycle-charge impact, peel-back, and subsequent regrouping. Uid8 (team 1's own cavalry by scenario order: spearmen, infantry, archers, cavalry, cavalry) is the deep block from the overlap exemption above (505.8wu spread, depth ratio 2.81) and never reaches melee over the whole clip (state stays MOVING, engaged false, through tick 1300): it's under a continuous AI ATTACK order whose target_enemy_uid re-selects mid-run (uid3 through tick 540, uid4 from tick 600, uid2 from tick 1200), and each retarget demands a sharp reorientation the deep block can't finish before the next one lands -- the slots-to-bodies fit angle swings from 4deg at tick 540 to 92deg at tick 600 (the 3->4 retarget), unwinds only to 30-46deg by tick 960-1140, then reverses again to -79deg at the 4->2 retarget (tick 1200). The shape-fit residual tracks that unfinished turn: 20.3wu at the first retarget (tick 600), climbing to worst=118.2wu at tick 900-960 (spacing 40wu x SHAPE_RMS_FRAC floor 30.0), and still 88.8wu at the clip's last sampled tick (1300) because the block is never left on one heading long enough to complete the fit before the AI moves the target again. Same AI chase-trajectory divergence already documented for uid7/uid8's overlap above, now visible as sustained shape scramble instead of compression; measured at the catalog cadence on this tree. This is read as the honest physics of a continuously-retargeting deep block with no reform order, not a formation-code defect -- whether the AI's retarget hysteresis should hold a heading longer before flipping is an open design question, tracked separately.

path_crossing.reason: Charging cavalry paths cross during the cycle-charge breakthrough, disengagement wheel, and realignment.
